source: KICD Social Studies, First Published 2017; Revised 2024 (text layer)
status: outcomes from KICD's text, word for word; skills, prerequisites and misconceptions not yet mapped

learning_experiences: brainstorm the four cardinal points of a compass,
draw and label the four cardinal points, practise giving directions to places using the four cardinal points,
use the four compass points to show direction on the interactive map to enrich the mapping skills.
play computer games on the compass direction for enjoyment.
key_inquiry_questions: How can we show direction of places?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Digital Literacy: Learners interact with digital devices as they play computer games on compass direction for enjoyment.
Learning to learn: Learners develop relationships as they share resources and practise giving direction of places using the four cardinal points.
sub_strands.values:
Unity: Learners cooperate as they practise giving direction of places using the four cardinal points.
Respect: Learners show patience as they play computer games on compass direction for enjoyment.
sub_strands.pcis: Creative Thinking: Learners participate in creative games as they play computer games on compass direction for enjoyment.
sub_strands.links: Learners use Creative Arts skills as they draw and label the four cardinal points.

outcomes.text: identify the four cardinal points of a compass
use the four cardinal points to give directions on a map
appreciate the use of four cardinal points in everyday life

sub_strands.sub_strand: Location and size of the County
learning_experiences: brainstorm and list sub-counties in their county,
use relevant print or digital resources to identify the location of the county in relation to neighbouring counties,
discuss the size of the county in relation to the neighbouring counties,
sketch, colour, and display the map of the county in class,
play games on the location of the county in relation to neighbouring counties.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is it important to learn the size and location of a county?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Digital Literacy: Learners develop simple games as they play games on the location of the county in relation to the neighbouring counties
Learning to learn: Learners search for the location and size of their county
sub_strands.values: Responsibility: Learners engage in assigned roles and duties as they discuss the size of the county in relation to the neighbouring counties
sub_strands.pcis:
Problem Solving: Learners play creative games as they locate the county in relation to the neigbouring counties
Effective Communication: Learners brainstorm to identify sub-counties in their county.
sub_strands.links: English: Learners apply listening and speaking skills as they discuss in groups the size of the county in relation to the neigbouring counties

outcomes.text: identify sub-counties in the county
locate the county in relation to neighbouring counties
estimate the size of the county in relation to neighbouring counties
acknowledge the location and size of the county

learning_experiences: brainstorm the main physical features in the county, sketch the main physical features in the county,
draw or take photographs of the main physical features in the county,
outline the importance of the main physical features in the county and share the discussion points in class,
display pictures or models of the main physical features in the county in class,
find out from parents or guardians the main physical features in the county and share.
key_inquiry_questions: Which physical features are found in your county?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Citizenship: Learners identify the main physical features in their county.
Learning to: Learners find out from parents or guardians the physical features in the county and share
sub_strands.values: Social Justice: Learners accord equal opportunities in sharing responsibilities as they outline the importance of the main physical features in the county and share the discussion points in class.
sub_strands.pcis: Self-Awareness: Learners appreciate each other’s abilities as they draw some of the main physical features in the county.
sub_strands.links: English: Learners use speaking skills as they discuss in groups the importance of the main physical features in the county in class.

outcomes.text: identify the main physical features in the county
state the importance of the main physical features in the county
illustrate the main physical features in the county
appreciate the main physical features in the county

learning_experiences: brainstorm about seasons experienced in the county,
use print or digital resources to identify seasons experienced in the county
engage a resource person to find out how seasons influence human activities in the county
discuss ways in which rainy weather affects safety of road users,
draw weather charts of seasons in the county,
observe and record in charts human activities associated with different seasons.
sing songs about seasons experienced in the county,
key_inquiry_questions: How do seasons influence human activities in the county?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Collaboration: Learners develop relationships as they brainstorm about seasons experienced in the county.
Digital Literacy: Learners use print or digital resources to identify seasons experienced in the county.
sub_strands.values:
Respect: Learners appreciate diverse opinions as they brainstorm about seasons experienced in the county.
Patriotism: Learners sing songs about seasons experienced in the county,
sub_strands.pcis: Safety and security: Learners discuss precautions to take during the different seasons experienced in the county (Hot, cold, dry and rainy season).
sub_strands.links: Agriculture: Learners explain how different seasons influence human activities in the county.

outcomes.text: identify the four seasons experienced in the county
explain how the four seasons influence human activities in the county
explore how rainy weather affects road safety in the county
model weather charts of seasons in the county
appreciate the different seasons experienced in the county

sub_strands.sub_strand: Historic Built Environments in the County
learning_experiences: brainstorm and share the main historic built environments in the county,
use print or digital resources to identify historic built environments in the county,
visit some of the historic, built environments within the locality (take photographs, audio tape conversations on the environments or take notes),
engage a resource person to discuss the importance of the historic built environment in the county,
participate in conserving historic built environments in the locality as service learning (collecting litter, sweeping).
key_inquiry_questions: How can we care for the historic built environments in our county?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Critical thinking and problem solving: Learners participate in conserving historic built environments in the locality (collecting litter, sweeping).
Self-efficacy: Learners engage resource person to discuss the importance of historic built environments within the county.
sub_strands.values:
Unity: Learners participate in conserving historic built environments in the locality as service learning (collecting litter, sweeping).
Responsibility: Learners understands and appreciates the resource person as they discuss the importance of the historic built environment in the county
sub_strands.pcis: Environmental issues: Learners respect others' views/feelings as they visit some of the historic built environments in the locality (take photographs, audio tape conversations on the environments or take notes).
sub_strands.links: Learners use Creative Arts skills to create a picture booklet on the historic built environments.

outcomes.text: identify the main historic built environments in the county
explain the importance of the main historic built environments in the county
participate in conservation activities of the historic built environments within the county
appreciate historic built environments in the county

sub_strands.strand: People and Population Inter-dependence of people (6 Lessons)
learning_experiences: brainstorm in class the ways in which people depend on each other in the county,
use print or digital resources to identify ways in which people depend on each other in the county,
draw a chart on benefits of interdependence among the people,
role-play interdependence of people in the community,
recite a poem about the importance of interdependence of people,
find out from parents or guardians about the importance of interdependence of people and report back.
key_inquiry_questions: How do people in the county depend on each other?
Why should we support each other in the county?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Citizenship: Learners explain the benefits of interdependence of people in the county.
Creativity and imagination: Learners role-play the interdependence of people in the county.
sub_strands.values: Social justice: Learners discuss benefits of interdependence among people in the county
sub_strands.pcis:
Social cohesion: Learners identify ways in which people depend on each other in the county.
Social cohesion: Learners respect others’ views/feelings as they work to create a chart on benefits of interdependence among people.
sub_strands.links:
English: Learners develop communication skills as they recite a poem about the importance of interdependence of people.
Religious Education: Learners explain the importance of interdependence.

outcomes.text: identify ways in which people depend on each other in the county
explain the benefits of interdependence of people in the county
use chart to illustrate the benefits of interdependence people
appreciate the interdependence of people in the County

sub_strands.strand: People and Population Inter-dependence of people (6 Lessons)
learning_experiences: brainstorm what is population distribution,
use a digital or print map of the county to identify the patterns of population, distribution in the county,
explain the patterns of population distribution in the county,
use the map of the county to plot patterns of population distribution,
draw a map of the county showing population distribution,
display the map of the county in the appropriate learning corner.
key_inquiry_questions: How is population spread out in the county?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Digital Literacy: Learners use a digital or print map of the county to identify the patterns of population distribution.
Learning to Learn: Learners develop relationships as they share diagrams of the patterns of population distribution in class.
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: Learners develop self-drive as they share the diagrams of the patterns of population distribution in class.
Integrity: Learners have self-discipline as they use a digital or print map of the county to identify the patterns of population distribution.
sub_strands.pcis:
Critical thinking and problem solving: Learners ask challenging questions as they share the diagrams of the patterns of population distribution in class.
Effective Communication: Learners use appropriate communication channel as they discuss population distribution in the county.
sub_strands.links:
Learners apply listening and speaking skills as they discuss population distribution in the county.
Learners apply Creative Arts skills as they draw a map of the county showing population distribution.

outcomes.text: describe patterns of population distribution in the county
illustrate the patterns of population distribution in the county
appreciate population distribution in the county

sub_strands.sub_strand: Aspects of Traditional Culture in the County.
learning_experiences: brainstorm aspects of traditional culture in the county,
describe aspects of traditional culture in the county,
discuss the importance of traditional culture in the county,
collect and record aspects of traditional culture practised in the community (pictures, songs, artefacts, dress, food, paintings, tools),
showcase different aspects of traditional culture practised in the community.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is culture important?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Creativity and imagination: Learners showcase different aspects of traditional culture practised in the community.
Citizenship: Learners collect and record aspects of traditional culture practised in the community.
sub_strands.values: Respect: Learners recognise different aspects of traditional culture in their county.
sub_strands.pcis: Self-Awareness: Learners appreciate individual uniqueness as they describe aspects of traditional culture in their county.
sub_strands.links: Creative Arts: Learners will apply skills drawn from showcasing different aspects of traditional culture practised in the community in Creative Arts.

outcomes.text: identify aspects of traditional culture in the county
illustrate aspects of traditional culture practised in the county
appreciate the importance of traditional culture in the county

learning_experiences: gather information on the history of the school from relevant personnel and share in class,
discuss the history of the school with others in class,
use digital or print resources to find out the school values,
develop a poster on the school values
develop a poster on the school motto and display it in class,
make a gallery walk and peer assess.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is it important to maintain discipline in school?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and collaboration: Learners recite the school motto
Citizenship: Learners gather information on the history of the school from the school administration and share in class
sub_strands.values: Integrity: Learners exhibit discipline as they display, make a gallery walk and peer assess.
sub_strands.pcis: Social cohesion: Learners develop charts to explain the school values
sub_strands.links: Creative arts: Learners apply graphic designing in Creative Arts in the designing of school motto and rules

outcomes.text: narrate the history of the school
explain the values of the school
recite the school motto
desire to obey the school rules

learning_experiences: brainstorm on the economic activities in the county,
make posters on the economic activities carried out in the county,
discuss the importance of economic activities in the county,
participate in appropriate economic activities in the locality,
create and recite poems or songs on the economic activities in their county.
key_inquiry_questions: How can we conserve the resources found in the county?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Collaboration: Learners participate in appropriate economic activities in the locality.
Learning to Learn: Learners shares ideas and make posters on the economic activities carried out in the county
sub_strands.values: Patriotism: Learners participate in the economic activities in the locality
sub_strands.pcis: Creative and critical thinking: Learners create and recite poems or songs on the economic activities in their county
sub_strands.links:
Agriculture: learners participate in economic activities
Pre-technical Studies: Learners identify the importance of economic activities

outcomes.text: Explore the main resources found in the county
identify the main economic activities carried out in the county
explain the importance of economic activities carried out in the county
participate in economic activities in the locality
appreciate the economic activities in the county

learning_experiences: share the industries in the county,
discuss the benefits of industries in the county,
locate industries in the county,
visit an industry to learn its benefits in the county,
create a poster of the industry visited and display in class,
Compose poems on the benefits of industries in the county.
key_inquiry_questions: How can a county benefit from its industries?
sub_strands.core_competences: Creativity: Learners create a poster of the industry visited and display in class
sub_strands.values:
Patriotism: Learners portray citizenship as they visit an industry to learn about its benefits in the county.
Integrity: Learners develop honesty as they utilise resources prudently while creating a poster of the industry visited and displaying in class
sub_strands.pcis: Safety: Learners exercise caution as they visit an industry to learn its benefits in the county.
sub_strands.links: Science and Technology: Learners explain benefits of industries in the county

outcomes.text: identify industries in the county
explain the benefits of industries in the county
locate industries in the county
recognise the role of industries in the county

learning_experiences: brainstorm enterprise projects that can be undertaken at school,
plan and undertake a viable enterprise project at school,
design personal protective equipment for safety on the roads using locally available materials,
participate in the initiation and management of the enterprise project in the school,
share responsibilities on the planned enterprise project,
discuss ethical practices to be observed in managing the enterprise project,
showcase the school project.
key_inquiry_questions: How are enterprise projects managed in school?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and collaboration: Learners share responsibilities on the planned enterprise
Creativity and imagination: Learners identify a viable project enterprise at school
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: Learners engage in the assigned roles and duties as they undertake the enterprise project at school and evaluate its success
Integrity: Learners develop accountability as they participate in the initiation and management of the enterprise project in the school
sub_strands.pcis: Creative and critical thinking: Learners undertake the enterprise project at school and showcase the outcomes.
sub_strands.links: Mathematics: Learners plan and undertake a viable enterprise project at school.

outcomes.text: identify the projects that can be initiated at school
participate in initiating an enterprise project at school
uphold ethics and collective efforts in managing enterprise projects at school

sub_strands.strand: Citizenship and Governance in Kenya STRAND 1.0: NATURAL AND BUILT ENVIRONMENTS
learning_experiences: brainstorm qualities of a good citizen in school,
use digital or print resources to identify qualities of a good citizen in school,
role-play qualities of a good citizen in a school,
engage a role model in the community and discuss good citizenship,
design a poster with qualities of a good citizen in school,
write an essay on qualities of a good citizen and share in class.
key_inquiry_questions: How can we demonstrate good citizenship in school?
sub_strands.core_competences: Citizenship: Learners role-play qualities of a good citizen in school
sub_strands.values: Unity: Learners design a poster with qualities of a good citizen in school
sub_strands.pcis: Social cohesion: Learners develop harmonious coexistence as they discuss how to become a good citizen in school
sub_strands.links: English: Learners apply writing skills as they write an essay on a good digital citizen (using technology in a positive way) and share the essays in class.

outcomes.text: identify qualities of a good citizen in school
develop qualities of good citizenship in school
appreciate qualities of good citizenship in school

sub_strands.strand: Citizenship and Governance in Kenya STRAND 1.0: NATURAL AND BUILT ENVIRONMENTS
learning_experiences: discuss factors that promote peace in school,
create messages on strategies of living in peace with others in school,
use digital or print resources to find out examples of peace activities undertaken in schools (peace gardens/nature trails, peace corners, peace competition essays),
design posters with peace-building messages,
participate in peacebuilding activities
find out from parents and guardians how they can uphold peace.
key_inquiry_questions: How can we live in peace with others in school?
Why is it important to plan for a peacebuilding activity in school?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Critical thinking: Learners create messages on strategies of living in peace with others in school.
Problem solving: Learners participate in peace building activities in school.
sub_strands.values:
Patriotism: Learners design posters with peacebuilding messages
Peace: Learners show respect as they participate in peacebuilding activities
sub_strands.pcis: Coping with emotions: Learners identify factors that promote peace in school
sub_strands.links: Religious Education: Learners apply religious concept of peace as they discuss ways of promoting peace in school

outcomes.text: identify factors that promote peace in school
develop strategies of living in peace with others in school
desire to uphold peace in school

sub_strands.strand: Citizenship and Governance in Kenya STRAND 1.0: NATURAL AND BUILT ENVIRONMENTS
content_topics: Abuse of children with special needs
learning_experiences: brainstorm forms of child abuse in the community,
use digital or print resources to find out the causes of child abuse in the community,
discuss effects of child abuse in the community,
design posters on the effects of child abuse in the community,
sing songs and recite poems on the protection of self and others from child abuse in the community,
create awareness on use of authorised school transport practices to peers,
participate in activities that promote child rights in the school.
key_inquiry_questions: How can harmful cultural practices violate child rights in the community?
How can we protect ourselves from child abuse?
sub_strands.core_competences: Self-Efficacy: Learners participate in activities that promote child rights in the school
sub_strands.values: Responsibility: Learners design posters on the effects of child abuse in the community,
sub_strands.pcis: Gender Issues: Learners identify the causes of child abuse in the community.
sub_strands.links: Religious Education: Learners participate in activities that promote child rights in the school.

outcomes.text: outline forms of child abuse in the community
explain the causes of child abuse in the community
explain effects of child abuse in the community
desire to promote child rights and responsibilities in the school

sub_strands.strand: Citizenship and Governance in Kenya STRAND 1.0: NATURAL AND BUILT ENVIRONMENTS
learning_experiences: brainstorm democratic processes in school,
prepare a chart showing the democratic processes in the school,
discuss benefits of democracy in school,
prepare posters with benefits of democracy in school,
carry out a mock election of leaders in class,
engage a resource person to learn the elements of democratic practices in school.
key_inquiry_questions: How can we practise democracy in school?
Why is democracy important in a school?
sub_strands.core_competences: Learning to learn: Learners prepare a chart showing the democratic processes in the school,
sub_strands.values: Unity: Learners develop inclusivity and respect others’ opinions as they discuss benefits of democracy in school.
sub_strands.pcis: Social cohesion: Learners develop harmonious coexistence as they carry out a mock election of leaders in class
sub_strands.links: Creative Arts: Learners prepare posters with the benefits of democracy in school

outcomes.text: identify democratic processes in the school
explain the benefits of democracy in school
practise democratic elements in school
appreciate democratic practices in school

sub_strands.strand: Citizenship and Governance in Kenya STRAND 1.0: NATURAL AND BUILT ENVIRONMENTS
learning_experiences: brainstorm the composition of Children’s Government in school,
write the structure of the Children’s Government,
share experiences in groups on functions of Children’s Government in school,
role-play the functions of Children’s Government,
write a composition on ways of participating in Children’s Government in school,
simulate the Children’s Government in session in school,
share on how to respect Children’s Government.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is it important to have a Children's Government in school?
How can we support Children’s Government in school?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Citizenship: citizenship is developed as learners simulate the Children’s Government in session in school,
Collaboration: Learners share experiences on functions of Children’s Government in school.
sub_strands.values:
Integrity: Learners simulate the Children’s Government in session in school
Social Justice: Learners accord privileges without favour as they role-play the functions of Children’s Government
sub_strands.pcis: Governance: Learners describe the functions of Children’s Government in school
sub_strands.links: Learners apply writing skills as they write a composition on ways of supporting Children’s Government in school.

outcomes.text: explain the composition of Children’s Government in school
describe the functions of the Children’s Government in school
participate in Children’s Government in school
respect Children’s Government in school

sub_strands.strand: Citizenship and Governance in Kenya STRAND 1.0: NATURAL AND BUILT ENVIRONMENTS
learning_experiences: name leaders in the community
discuss duties of community leaders and make class presentation,
engage a resource person to discuss the qualities of a good community leader and report,
role-play qualities of good leadership in the community,
design and display a poster with qualities of good leadership in the community,
Compose songs on good leadership in the community.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is it important for leaders to have good qualities?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Creativity: Learners design and display a poster with qualities of good leadership in the community,
Learning to learn: Learners engage a resource person to discuss the qualities of a good community leader and report.
sub_strands.values: Integrity: Learners role-play qualities of good leadership in the community.
sub_strands.pcis: Leadership: Learners engage a resource person to discuss the qualities of a good community leader and report.
sub_strands.links: Creative Arts as they design and display a poster with qualities of good leadership in the community.

outcomes.text: identify leaders in the community
explain the duties of leaders in the community
demonstrate qualities of good leadership in the community
appreciate good leadership in the community

sub_strands.strand: Citizenship and Governance in Kenya STRAND 1.0: NATURAL AND BUILT ENVIRONMENTS
learning_experiences: brainstorm the leaders of county government in Kenya
outline the structure of the county government
draw the structure of the county assembly in Kenya
discuss the duties of the governor and a member of the county assembly,
watch video clips or visit county government offices to learn administrative structure.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is a county government important in Kenya?
What are the duties of ward and village administrators?
sub_strands.core_competences: Learning to Learn: Learners engage a resource person to discuss duties of the governor and the roles of a member of county assembly
sub_strands.values: Respect: Learners understand and appreciate leaders as they discuss in groups the roles of members of the county assembly (MCAs)
sub_strands.pcis: Governance: Learners learn the structure of county government and discuss the duties of the governor and members of the county assembly,
sub_strands.links: Creative Arts: as learners draw the structure of the county government

outcomes.text: identify the structure of county government
explain the duties of County Governor in Kenya
explain the roles of a member of county assembly
appreciate the County Government in Kenya
